causal_chain: A separate veto channel can learn which historical interactions imply mismatch or substitution conflict for that same candidate, producing explicit subtractive evidence instead of forcing all disagreement into weak low-affinity scores.

Because held-out ranking on ML-1M contains many users with mixed histories, separating support from veto and enforcing support robustness should improve ranking of candidates that are locally consistent with part of a user's taste while suppressing candidates that only match popularity or the wrong taste facet.

Candidate-conditioned cross-attention over a user's historical items can identify which past interactions provide positive evidence for a queried candidate rather than collapsing all history into one static user vector.

Training the model to preserve pairwise margins when its top support evidences are partially masked discourages brittle reliance on one shortcut co-occurrence and promotes distributed collaborative support.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or a generic history-attention effect rather than from the specific dual support-versus-veto decomposition and support-masking stability objective.
discriminative_predictions: If performance gains are only due to popularity smoothing or extra capacity, improvements should concentrate on head items and should not persist under a parameter-matched attentive additive-history control without the veto channel and masking objective.

If support-robustness is causal, the proposed model should show smaller NDCG@10 degradation than a matched attentive-history control when a few high-attention historical interactions are ablated at evaluation-time scoring.

If the support/veto decomposition is causal, removing only the veto channel while keeping parameter count similar should reduce improvement most strongly for users with diverse or internally conflicting histories.
expected_evidence: Ablation of the support-masking stability term reduces robustness to history-item removal and weakens any ranking gain on mixed-taste users.
Compared with a parameter-matched attentive-history pairwise control, the full model improves full-sort NDCG@10 on the frozen ML-1M split.
Dual-channel attention diagnostics show that promoted and vetoed history items differ systematically for the same user-candidate pair rather than collapsing to the same support pattern.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a parameter-matched control that uses candidate-conditioned history attention but no explicit veto channel and no support-masking stability matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, the frontier claim is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is not a parameter or tuning variation of BPR_MF or existing LightGCN descendants. It changes the scoring object from static user-item compatibility to candidate-conditioned evidence routing over user history, introduces a new negative collaborative relation via veto evidence, and adds a counterfactual stability objective requiring custom executable logic beyond current profile operators.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that scores each user-item pair through dual candidate-conditioned set encoders over the user's interaction history—one promotive support channel and one subtractive veto channel—and that regularizes pairwise margins to remain stable under masking of top support interactions will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static pairwise collaborative filters on the frozen ML-1M protocol.
implementation_requirements: Add a support-masking consistency term that recomputes the positive-item score after masking a small subset of highest-support history items and penalizes excessive pairwise margin collapse.
Define score(u,i)=base_user_item_affinity + support_score(u,i) - veto_score(u,i), with pairwise BPR-style loss on positive and sampled negative items.
Implement a RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise training that caches each user's train-history item indices and a padded/truncated history tensor for minibatch lookup.
Provide candidate-local ablations for mechanism-off execution: no-veto/no-mask attentive control and optionally no-mask full model using the same training/evaluation pipeline.
Use shared item embeddings plus lightweight support-query and veto-query projections so a target item attends over a user's history twice, producing promotive and subtractive evidence summaries.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a parameter-matched candidate-conditioned attentive-history pairwise recommender with the same embedding tables, history truncation, optimizer, and training loop, but collapse evidence to a single additive support channel and remove the support-masking consistency loss.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace static user representation scoring with dual candidate-conditioned historical evidence routing and counterfactual support-stability regularization.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off variant: keep the same item embeddings, candidate-conditioned history lookup, and pairwise training loop, but disable the veto channel and the support-masking consistency loss so scoring becomes base_user_item_affinity plus a single additive support-attention summary only.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A dual-channel candidate-conditioned history-attention BPR recommender versus a parameter-matched single-channel attentive-history BPR control under identical frozen ML-1M full-sort evaluation.
blind_projection.research_question: Does explicitly separating promotive and veto historical evidence for each candidate, plus enforcing support-robust pairwise margins, improve full-sort NDCG@10 beyond what can be achieved by ordinary static compatibility or single-channel attentive-history collaborative filtering under the frozen ML-1M protocol?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A truncated-history implementation with shared projections and one masked re-score per positive pair should fit the development budget on ML-1M, because the dataset is moderate and the model avoids full graph propagation or large transformer stacks.
